title: Write path: INSERT with WITH CHECK, UPDATE and DELETE of the subject's own rows, RETURNING and UPDATE ... FROM
issue: RLS checks every written row: USING on the old row, WITH CHECK on the new row, plus the SELECT policy for UPDATE/RETURNING. With per-command policies on an indexed tenant column that is one InitPlan comparison per row; pg_auth does the same through authz.permits (WITH CHECK equivalent) and a role-aware write permission. Also probes where the two diverge (a row-id object cannot authorise an INSERT because its OpenFGA tuple does not exist yet).
symptom: best_practice_rls and pg_auth should cost about the same per written row; naive_rls (unwrapped auth.jwt() in WITH CHECK) pays JSON parsing per inserted row. The pg_auth_row_object variant answers 'denied' for inserts that RLS allows.

scale.meaning: number of rows in app.tasks. 30% belong to one large tenant; the rest spread over scale/500 tenants (min 20), 5 projects per tenant (one in five archived), 3 users per tenant (the third is a read-only viewer), app.drafts has least(scale/20, 5000) rows. 10x = 200,000 tasks, 400 tenants; OpenFGA tuples grow with members (3 per tenant) and drafts (capped at 5000), not with tasks.
